prediction:
THOUGHT: Patient is a genetically female adolescent with primary amenorrhea, lack of breast development (Tanner I) but a normal uterus and ovaries on ultrasound, tall stature and history of low-trauma fractures — all pointing to estrogen deficiency with intact internal female organs. Virilization at birth (clitoromegaly, partial labial fusion) plus maternal virilization during pregnancy indicate excess fetal/placental androgen production that also affected the mother in utero. Ongoing severe acne and ovarian cysts fit continued androgen excess. These features are classic for placental aromatase deficiency (CYP19A1 mutation): fetal inability to convert androgens to estrogens causes virilization of an XX fetus and virilization of the mother during pregnancy; postnatally the child has androgen excess but little estrogen (explaining lack of breast development, tall stature from delayed epiphyseal closure, and osteoporotic fractures). Alternatives (21‑hydroxylase CAH, complete androgen insensitivity) are less consistent because CAH usually does not cause maternal virilization and typically leads to earlier epiphyseal closure/short stature, while complete AIS has absent uterus and normal breast development. Confirmation would be by elevated androgens with low estrogens, 46,XX karyotype, and genetic testing for CYP19A1 mutation.  
DIAGNOSIS: Aromatase (placental) deficiency (CYP19A1 mutation)
